questions.question: State and prove the work-energy theorem for a constant force.
questions.solution:

questions.question: A body of mass 4 kg is released from rest and falls freely through a height of 10 m. Take $g = 9.8\ \text{m/s}^2$ and find the kinetic energy and speed of the body just before striking the ground.
questions.solution:
**Step 1 — By the law of conservation of energy,** the loss of gravitational potential energy equals the gain in kinetic energy:
$$mgh = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$$

**Step 2 — Kinetic energy:**
$$KE = mgh = 4 \times 9.8 \times 10 = 392\ \text{J}$$
$$\boxed{KE = \mathbf{392\ \text{J}}$$

**Step 3 — Speed:**
$$\frac{1}{2}mv^2 = mgh \;\Rightarrow\; v = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{2 \times 9.8 \times 10} = \sqrt{196}$$
$$\boxed{v = \mathbf{14\ \text{m/s}}}$$

**Step 4 — Check:** $\frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 14^2 = 2 \times 196 = 392\ \text{J}$ ✓ (independent of mass, as expected for free fall).
questions.knowledgeNote: In free fall, mgh equals half mv squared, giving v equals square root of 2gh independent of mass.
